title: Data Augmentation using Large Language Models: Data Perspectives, Learning Paradigms and Challenges
extended_summary:
This paper is a survey of data augmentation methods using large language models (LLMs). It focuses on how LLMs are changing data augmentation from both a data-centric perspective and a learning-paradigm perspective, rather than evaluating a specific educational intervention or user study. The paper organizes the literature into categories such as data creation, data labeling, data reformation, and co-annotation, and then further distinguishes generative learning and discriminative learning settings.

The central question is how LLMs can be used to create, label, transform, or score data in ways that improve downstream machine learning performance. The survey discusses examples across NLP and some multimodal tasks, including instruction tuning, in-context learning, alignment learning, classification, regression, and counterfactual generation. It also reviews major concerns such as contamination, controllability, cultural bias, multimodal complexity, and privacy risks.

The paper does not study a student population, classroom use, or any K-12 literacy intervention. Instead, it synthesizes prior computational research and proposes a taxonomy and future directions for LLM-based data augmentation. Its main conclusion is that LLMs substantially expand the possibilities for synthetic data generation and annotation, but careful handling is needed to address quality, contamination, bias, and privacy issues.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic large language model-based generative AI used for data augmentation, annotation, rephrasing, instruction generation, and evaluation tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: This is a survey of large language model (LLM)-based data augmentation methods. It reviews how generic LLMs are used to create synthetic data, label datasets, reformulate text, and provide annotations or scores across NLP and other domains.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a survey/review paper with no original empirical evaluation of a student-facing AI tool. It summarizes prior work on LLM-based data augmentation rather than reporting a controlled study or meta-analytic estimate.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper does not test an intervention in K-12 reading or literacy instruction and reports no outcome effects. Its relevance is conceptual only for the stated education research topic.
